chunks: And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Udaym ibn al-Ḥurr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees: is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: Yes. And do not tell them, lest they take it as a pretext.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the legal ruling
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required after a state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.نَعَمْ: an affirmative answer establishing the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she experiences a nocturnal emission in her sleep?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a woman experiences discharge in sleep in the manner that necessitates ritual impurity, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her. It also adds an instruction not to publicize this to women in a way that would lead some to use it as an excuse or pretext.
